correctness.rationale: The published V-description fixes the sign of every nonzero coordinate, so squared Euclidean distance is exactly support Hamming distance. Each matching selects at most one coordinate in each maximal run. The two-vertex optimization therefore has three symmetric open-matching states. The four singleton/spare run transition tables are exhaustive, and a direct induction solves their max-plus product as A_i=2i+2g_i, B_i=A_i+2h_i-1, C_i=A_i+2h_i-2. The terminal closed state gives diameter squared 2(f+g). The independent zero-vertex argument gives eccentricity sqrt(2f) and the product count of extremal vertices. A full polytope diameter is attained at a vertex pair, so no nonvertex case is omitted.

value.rationale: Shard polytopes are the elementary building blocks in the source's Minkowski construction of quotientopes and have an active later literature through matroid and Ehrhart interpretations. Euclidean diameter is a canonical realization-sensitive size invariant. The theorem compresses its exact value to two transparent arc statistics, shows that run lengths beyond one versus at least two are metrically irrelevant for diameter, gives sharp universal bounds and equality conditions, and also determines the complete farthest-from-zero count. This is a structural all-arc classification rather than a finite example or routine parameter increment.
